record.paper_title: Notes on open questions within density functional theory (existence of a derivative of the Lieb functional in a restricted sense and non-interacting v-representability)
record.context_brief: Exact non-interacting representability of interacting densities
record.original_question: Is the non-interacting v-representability conjecture true, meaning that every interacting ensemble v-representable ground-state density in the set B can be reproduced exactly by some non-interacting Kohn-Sham system, so that B equals the set Bs of non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities? Equivalently, when a sequence of non-interacting densities nε in Bs converges to an interacting density n in B, does the limit always correspond to an actually attainable non-interacting density rather than merely an arbitrarily good approximation?

evidence.quote: Now, even if the Lieb functional could be proven admit a derivative in a restricted sense, a further difficulty may occur: the interacting and non-interacting Lieb functionals may not be differentiable on the same set. This difficulty has been called "non-interacting v-representability question"

There is (even conjecturing that a KS potential can rigorously be defined from the Lieb functional) no proof that the sets B and Bs are equal. Considering B = Bs, important for the complete foundation of the Lieb functional-based KS scheme, thus represents a further conjecture called "non-interacting v-representability conjecture".

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Setup. Consider an N-electron system on R^3. Let B denote the set of one-particle densities n ≥ 0 with ∫n = N that are ensemble v-representable for the interacting Hamiltonian H_v = T + W + Σ v(x_i), i.e. there exists an external potential v (in an appropriate class such as L^{3/2} + L^∞) and a ground-state ensemble of H_v whose one-particle density equals n. Let B_s denote the analogous set of non-interacting ensemble v-representable densities: those n for which there exists v_s such that some ground-state ensemble of the non-interacting Hamiltonian H_{v_s}^0 = T + Σ v_s(x_i) yields density n.

The Lieb functional is defined by the Legendre transform F[n] = sup_v { E(v) − ∫ v n }, where E(v) is the ground-state energy, and analogously F_s[n] for the non-interacting problem. A density n is in B (resp. B_s) iff F (resp. F_s) is subdifferentiable at n with a potential as subgradient.

Question (non-interacting v-representability conjecture). Is it true that B = B_s? Equivalently, for every interacting ensemble v-representable ground-state density n ∈ B, does there exist a non-interacting Kohn–Sham potential v_s such that n is exactly the ground-state ensemble density of the non-interacting Hamiltonian with potential v_s? In particular, when a sequence of non-interacting v-representable densities n_ε ∈ B_s converges (in the natural density topology) to an interacting v-representable density n ∈ B, must the limit n itself lie in B_s (i.e. be exactly attainable as a non-interacting ground-state density), rather than only being approximable by such densities?
artifact.status_search_result: The non-interacting v-representability conjecture remains open in general. Recent works (2024–2025) on rigorous formulations of Kohn–Sham theory, distributional-potential v-representability on the 1D torus, and quantitative Hohenberg–Kohn theorems address related questions and obtain partial results in restricted settings, but the equality B = B_s in the general continuum setting has not been established. A 2019 result shows that, in the absence of degeneracy, an interacting pure-state v-representable density is non-interacting v-representable by a Slater determinant, a partial positive result.

status_evidence.title: Rigorous Formalization of Orbital Functionals: Addressing the Noninteracting v-Representability Problem
status_evidence.snippet: The overlap between interacting and noninteracting v-representability is poorly understood, which has direct implications for Kohn–Sham theory.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024, equality of interacting and non-interacting v-representable sets is not understood.

status_evidence.title: v-representability and Hohenberg-Kohn theorem for non-interacting Schrödinger operators with distributional potentials in the one-dimensional torus
status_evidence.snippet: establishing the uniqueness of the Kohn-Sham density-to-potential map and the differentiability of the non-interacting convex Lieb functional
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress for non-interacting v-representability in a restricted 1D setting.

status_evidence.title: Is an interacting ground state (pure state) v-representable density also non-interacting ground state v-representable by a Slater determinant? In the absence of degeneracy, yes!
status_evidence.snippet: In the absence of degeneracy, yes!
status_evidence.claim: Partial affirmative result in the non-degenerate pure-state case.
